title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 4 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ecclesiastes chapter 4 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 4 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ecclesiastes Chapter 4.

questions.question: What did the author consider when he returned according to Ecclesiastes 4:1?
options: All the oppressions that are done under the sun
questions.correctAnswer: All the oppressions that are done under the sun
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:1 states that the author considered all the oppressions done under the sun.

questions.question: Who did the author praise more than the living according to Ecclesiastes 4:2?
options: The dead which are already dead
questions.correctAnswer: The dead which are already dead
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:2 says the author praised the dead which are already dead more than the living which are yet alive.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 4:3, who is better than both the living and the dead?
options: He that hath not yet been
questions.correctAnswer: He that hath not yet been
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:3 states that better is he than both they, which hath not yet been.

questions.question: What causes a man to be envied by his neighbor according to Ecclesiastes 4:4?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:4 says that every right work and travail is envied by a man's neighbour.

questions.question: What does the fool do according to Ecclesiastes 4:5?
options: Foldeth his hands together, and eateth his own flesh
questions.correctAnswer: Foldeth his hands together, and eateth his own flesh
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:5 describes the fool as folding his hands and eating his own flesh.

questions.question: Which is better according to Ecclesiastes 4:6?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:6 states better is an handful with quietness than both the hands full with travail and vexation of spirit.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 4:1 mentions that the oppressed had no comforter.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:1 clearly states the oppressed had no comforter.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 4:2 praises the living more than the dead.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:2 praises the dead which are already dead more than the living.

questions.question: True or False: According to Ecclesiastes 4:3, it is better to have seen the evil work done under the sun.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:3 says better is he who hath not seen the evil work done under the sun.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 4:6 suggests that having much labor and vexation is preferable to quietness with little.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:6 states better is an handful with quietness than both hands full with travail and vexation.

questions.question: What did the author observe about the oppressors in Ecclesiastes 4:1?
options: They had power but no comforter
They were comforters to the oppressed
They were kind to the oppressed
questions.correctAnswer: They had power but no comforter
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:1 says on the side of the oppressors there was power, but they had no comforter.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 4:4, what is the result of a man’s travail and right work?
options: He is envied by his neighbour
questions.correctAnswer: He is envied by his neighbour
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:4 says a man is envied by his neighbour for his travail and right work.

questions.question: Which comes first in Ecclesiastes 4: the praise of the dead or the observation of travail and envy?
questions.explanation: Praise of the dead is mentioned in Ecclesiastes 4:2, which comes before the observation of travail and envy in 4:4.

questions.question: What is described as vanity and vexation of spirit in Ecclesiastes 4:4?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:4 calls travail and right work that causes envy vanity and vexation of spirit.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 4:5, what does the fool do with his hands?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:5 states the fool foldeth his hands together.

medium.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 4 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ecclesiastes Chapter 4 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 4:7, what does the author observe under the sun?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:7 states explicitly that the author saw vanity under the sun, indicating the futility and emptiness observed in life.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 4:8 say about a person who is alone without children or siblings?
options: He has endless labor without satisfaction
He is blessed with riches and peace
He is content with his work
questions.correctAnswer: He has endless labor without satisfaction
questions.explanation: Verse 8 describes a solitary person who labors endlessly without satisfaction, neither his eye nor his soul is content with riches, showing the vanity in solitary toil.

questions.question: How does Ecclesiastes 4:9 describe the benefit of two people working together?
options: They receive a good reward for their labor
They will have double the trouble
questions.correctAnswer: They receive a good reward for their labor
questions.explanation: Verse 9 states that two are better than one because they obtain a good reward for their labor, highlighting the advantage of cooperation and partnership.

questions.question: What practical help does Ecclesiastes 4:10 say a companion provides when one falls?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:10 teaches that if one falls, the other can lift him up, illustrating the importance of mutual support and care among companions.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 4:11, what advantage do two people lying together have over one alone?
questions.explanation: Verse 11 states that two lying together have heat, symbolizing warmth and comfort that one alone cannot provide, emphasizing companionship's practical benefits.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 4:12 say about the strength of companionship when facing adversity?
options: Two can withstand an attacker, and a threefold cord is not quickly broken
questions.correctAnswer: Two can withstand an attacker, and a threefold cord is not quickly broken
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:12 uses the metaphor of a threefold cord to illustrate that companionship strengthens resilience against opposition.

questions.question: Based on Ecclesiastes 4:7-10, what biblical virtue is most emphasized through the teaching about companionship?
questions.explanation: Verses 7-10 emphasize the value of companionship in providing support, lifting up one another, and sharing the rewards of labor, reflecting the virtue of mutual encouragement.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 4:6 suggest is better than having both hands full with labor and vexation of spirit?
options: A large house with many servants
questions.explanation: Verse 6 teaches that it is better to have a little with peace and contentment than much with trouble and anxiety, highlighting the value of quietness over stress.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'a threefold cord is not quickly broken' in Ecclesiastes 4:12 teach us about relationships?
questions.explanation: Verse 12 uses the metaphor of a threefold cord to show how additional bonds increase strength and resilience, teaching the importance of strong, united relationships.

questions.question: What warning does Ecclesiastes 4:10 give about being alone when one falls?
options: Woe to him who has no one to help him up
questions.correctAnswer: Woe to him who has no one to help him up
questions.explanation: Verse 10 warns that being alone when one falls is dangerous because there is no one to lift him up, stressing the necessity of companionship and support.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 4:13, which is considered better?
questions.explanation: Verse 13 states that a poor and wise child is better than an old and foolish king who refuses admonishment, highlighting wisdom over status or wealth.

questions.question: What lesson about humility and new beginnings is found in Ecclesiastes 4:14?
options: Those who come out of prison to reign are better off than those born into a kingdom who become poor
Poverty is a punishment for sin
questions.correctAnswer: Those who come out of prison to reign are better off than those born into a kingdom who become poor
questions.explanation: Verse 14 contrasts the rise of one from prison to reign with the decline of one born into royalty to poverty, teaching that humility and new beginnings can lead to greater blessing than inherited status.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 4:15 reveal about the succession of leadership?
options: A second child will stand up in the stead of the first
Leadership always remains with the eldest
questions.correctAnswer: A second child will stand up in the stead of the first
questions.explanation: Verse 15 describes the reality that the living walk under the sun with a second child who will succeed the first, emphasizing the transient nature of leadership.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 4:16 indicate about human legacy and joy?
options: There is no end to people, but those who come after will not rejoice in past generations
questions.correctAnswer: There is no end to people, but those who come after will not rejoice in past generations
questions.explanation: Verse 16 states that although people continue endlessly, future generations will not rejoice in former ones, illustrating the vanity and vexation related to human legacy.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 4:11 teaches that one person alone can easily keep warm without help.
questions.explanation: Verse 11 explicitly states that two lying together have heat, but one alone cannot be warm, showing the limitation of solitude in practical needs.

hard.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 4 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ecclesiastes Chapter 4.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 4:13, who is considered better than an old and foolish king?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:13 states that 'Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished.' This verse contrasts wisdom and poverty with foolishness and old age in leadership.

questions.question: What significant life transition is described in Ecclesiastes 4:14?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:14 says, 'For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becometh poor.' This describes the reversal where someone from a lowly or oppressed state ascends to power.

questions.question: Ecclesiastes 4:15 mentions a 'second child' who stands up in his stead. What does this most likely symbolize?
questions.explanation: The verse states 'I considered all the living which walk under the sun, with the second child that shall stand up in his stead,' implying succession or replacement, typically by an heir or successor.

questions.question: What is the overall conclusion about people mentioned in Ecclesiastes 4:16?
options: There is no end to people, but they do not rejoice in their predecessors
People always rejoice in their ancestors
questions.correctAnswer: There is no end to people, but they do not rejoice in their predecessors
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:16 states, 'There is no end of all the people... they also that come after shall not rejoice in him,' emphasizing the fleeting remembrance and vanity of human life.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage echoes the theme of a poor but wise person prevailing over folly as seen in Ecclesiastes 4:13?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 4:7 says, 'Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom,' connecting to the value of wisdom over status or wealth highlighted in Ecclesiastes 4:13.

questions.question: Ecclesiastes 4:14 contrasts someone coming out of prison to reign with another who is born in the kingdom but becomes poor. What Old Testament figure does this foreshadow?
questions.explanation: Joseph's story in Genesis shows him rising from imprisonment to become ruler, paralleling Ecclesiastes 4:14's theme of reversal of fortunes.

questions.question: What literary device is most evident in Ecclesiastes 4:12, which states 'a threefold cord is not quickly broken'?
questions.explanation: The phrase uses metaphor to compare strength in unity to a threefold cord, implying that combined strength is much harder to break.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word for 'vanity' (hebel), often translated as 'vexation of spirit' or 'meaninglessness,' suggest about the author's view in Ecclesiastes 4:16?
options: Life is governed by strict justice
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'hebel' conveys breath or vapor, symbolizing transience and futility, which aligns with the author's view in Ecclesiastes 4:16.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of Ecclesiastes 4's emphasis on the value of companionship and mutual support?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:24-25 encourages believers not to neglect meeting together and to support one another, reflecting the companionship theme in Ecclesiastes 4:9-10.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 4:8 describes a person who is alone, without child or brother, yet satisfied with his endless labor and riches.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:8 states that the solitary person has endless labor but his eye is not satisfied with riches, and he questions for whom he labors, indicating dissatisfaction.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 4:6 teaches that it is better to have a little with quietness than much with labor and vexation of spirit.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:6 states, 'Better is an handful with quietness, than both the hands full with travail and vexation of spirit,' highlighting the value of peace over toil.

questions.question: Ecclesiastes 4:1 speaks of the oppressed having no comforter. Which Psalm similarly expresses comfort for the oppressed?
questions.explanation: Psalm 9:9 states, 'The Lord also will be a refuge for the oppressed,' offering comfort as contrasted with the lack of comfort in Ecclesiastes 4:1.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'a threefold cord is not quickly broken' in relation to ancient Near Eastern culture?
options: It symbolizes the strength of family or community ties
It refers to a common agricultural tool
It is a reference to a religious ritual
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the strength of family or community ties
questions.explanation: In ancient Near Eastern culture, cords or ropes symbolized strength and unity; a threefold cord metaphorically represents the power of combined relationships, as seen in Ecclesiastes 4:12.

questions.question: Ecclesiastes 4:5 uses the imagery of a fool folding his hands and eating his own flesh. What does this metaphor imply about laziness?
questions.explanation: The metaphor in Ecclesiastes 4:5 implies that laziness (folding hands) harms oneself as if eating one’s own flesh, indicating self-destructive consequences.

questions.question: Which theme in Ecclesiastes 4 reflects the concept of 'vanity' or 'hebel' as introduced earlier in the book (Ecclesiastes 1), and how does it develop in verses 7-8?
options: The futility of solitary labor and unending toil
The joy of companionship and friendship
The power of wealth and riches
questions.correctAnswer: The futility of solitary labor and unending toil
questions.explanation: Verses 7-8 emphasize the vanity of solitary work and endless labor without satisfaction, echoing the 'hebel' theme of meaninglessness introduced in Ecclesiastes 1.

theological.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 4 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ecclesiastes Chapter 4 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 4:1 highlight about the oppression of individuals under the sun?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:1 states that the oppressed have no comforter, highlighting the sorrow and lack of support for those who suffer oppression.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 4:2, who is praised more than the living?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:2 indicates that the dead are praised more than the living, suggesting a perspective that values the peace of death over the struggles of life.

questions.question: What is said to be better than both the living and the dead in Ecclesiastes 4:3?
options: One who has not yet been
questions.correctAnswer: One who has not yet been
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:3 states that better is he who has not yet been, as he has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun, reflecting on the burdens of existence.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 4:4 say about envy?
options: It is vanity and vexation of spirit
questions.correctAnswer: It is vanity and vexation of spirit
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:4 notes that envy resulting from a man's work is vanity and vexation of spirit, emphasizing the futility of such feelings.

questions.question: What metaphor does Ecclesiastes 4:5 use to describe a fool?
options: He folds his hands and eats his own flesh
questions.correctAnswer: He folds his hands and eats his own flesh
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:5 describes a fool as someone who folds his hands together, implying inactivity and self-destruction, which leads to ruin.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 4:6, what is better than having both hands full?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:6 states that having an handful with quietness is better than having both hands full with travail and vexation, highlighting the value of peace over abundance.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 4:8 reveal about a solitary individual?
options: They have no end to their labor
questions.correctAnswer: They have no end to their labor
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:8 describes a solitary person as having no end to their labor, indicating the emptiness of striving without companionship or purpose.

questions.question: What advantage do two have over one according to Ecclesiastes 4:9?
options: A good reward for their labor
questions.correctAnswer: A good reward for their labor
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:9 states that two are better than one because they have a good reward for their labor, emphasizing the benefits of partnership.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 4:12, what is said about a threefold cord?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:12 indicates that a threefold cord is not quickly broken, symbolizing the strength found in unity and companionship.

questions.question: What insight does Ecclesiastes 4:13 give regarding a wise child?
options: They are better than a foolish king
questions.correctAnswer: They are better than a foolish king
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:13 asserts that a poor and wise child is better than an old and foolish king, highlighting the value of wisdom over status.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 4:14 teach about those who come out of prison?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:14 teaches that one who comes out of prison may come to reign, illustrating the potential for restoration and elevation despite past hardship.

questions.question: How does Ecclesiastes 4:16 describe the people who come after the living?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 4:16 indicates that those who come after the living will not rejoice in them, reflecting the vanity of human endeavors and memory.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 10 and 12 convey about companionship?
options: Two can help each other, and together they are strong
questions.correctAnswer: Two can help each other, and together they are strong
questions.explanation: Verses 10 and 12 together emphasize that companionship provides support in times of trouble and strength, as two can lift each other up and withstand challenges.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight is revealed when comparing Ecclesiastes 4:6 and 4:9?
options: The value of peace and companionship outweighs material gain
questions.correctAnswer: The value of peace and companionship outweighs material gain
questions.explanation: The comparison of verses 6 and 9 highlights that having peace and companionship is more valuable than the mere accumulation of wealth, reinforcing the theme of contentment.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 4:1-3 collectively teach about the condition of humanity?
options: Humanity suffers under oppression and longs for peace
Death is the end of all pain
questions.correctAnswer: Humanity suffers under oppression and longs for peace
questions.explanation: Verses 1-3 collectively convey the sorrow of humanity under oppression and the lack of comfort, suggesting a deep longing for peace that transcends life's struggles.
